lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.quote: An unrelated lawful ground for detention must be examined separately.
lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.note: The required Traps to Watch For section has been added.

lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.quote: A **quasi-judicial body** is an agency outside the courts that hears facts and decides certain disputes.
lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.note: All five named missing terms receive local plain definitions before applications.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: This does not excuse a separate crime.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Belief-only detention is distinguished from separate criminal conduct and worked in Example 1.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: An accusation alone is not a conviction.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Forced service and the due-conviction exception are explained and worked.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: Section $19$ forbids excessive fines and cruel, degrading, or inhuman punishment.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Excessive fines, prisoner protections, current death prohibition, replacement penalties, and parole are covered.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: A lawful conviction does not give officials permission to abuse a prisoner.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Abusive punishment and detention conditions are taught with evidence-based analysis and statutory penalty rules.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: Conviction or acquittal under either bars another prosecution under the other for the same act.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Same-offense conditions and the separate law/ordinance rule are both taught.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: An **ex post facto law** applies a harmful criminal-law change backward.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Meaning, harmful changes, limits, and two applications are provided.
Legislative punishment without a court trial is defined and applied in Example 16.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: Use available evidence, such as records, witness accounts, or medical findings.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: The method connects acts, evidence, rights, exceptions, and responsible officials.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: The missed work harms the family's income and ability to meet daily needs.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Example 18 derives individual and family effects only from supplied facts.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: A lawyer can assess a petition for a writ of habeas corpus.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Legal aid, court examination of detention, CHR investigation, and limits of office powers are taught.

lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.quote: Filing a complaint alone does not meet these conditions.
lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.note: Double jeopardy now has operational conditions and multiple worked applications.
